title: DMC3 HD Resource Volume Bootstrap and Mount Precedence — Phase 14

records.title: DMC3 resource bootstrap targets the executable-relative data/dmc3 directory and DMC3-N.nbz family
records.summary: The canonical bootstrap derives the executable directory, appends the literal \data\dmc3\ suffix, registers that physical root, and formats archive candidates with the literal %sDMC3-%d.nbz pattern.

locations.note: VA 0x14002E930. Builds the executable-relative data root, registers the physical root, then enters the numbered NBZ probe/mount loop.
VA 0x14036E920: literal \data\dmc3\ including the terminating NUL.
VA 0x14036E930: literal %sDMC3-%d.nbz including the terminating NUL.

records.title: Numbered NBZ probing starts at zero and stops at the first missing volume
records.summary: The bootstrap initializes the archive index to 0, formats DMC3-0.nbz, checks existence, mounts it when present, increments the index and repeats. A failed existence check exits the loop immediately, so later numbered archives after the first gap are not runtime-mounted by this bootstrap.

locations.note: VA 0x14002E930. The loop uses EBX=0 as the first %d argument, calls the existence helper, mounts on success, INC EBX, formats the next path, and exits on the first zero result.
VA 0x140327720. The helper returns false for ordinary missing/path-not-found outcomes used to terminate the bootstrap probe.

records.title: Physical and archive mounts are prepended to one global mount list
records.summary: Both the physical-root registration helper and the archive registration helper read the current global mount head, store it in the new node at +0x50, then replace the global head with the new node. The bootstrap registers the physical root before the numbered archives, so each later archive is placed ahead of every earlier mount.

locations.note: VA 0x140326D20. New physical node stores the prior global head at node+0x50 and becomes the new head. Bootstrap calls this before any numbered NBZ archive is added.
VA 0x140326DA0. Successful ZIP/NBZ archive node stores the prior global head at node+0x50 and becomes the new head.
VA 0x140CF3180. Zero-initialized runtime global head used by physical mount registration, archive mount registration and resolution traversal.

records.title: Effective archive resolution order is highest contiguous volume index down to zero
records.summary: The resolver begins at the global mount-list head and advances through node+0x50. Combined with ascending registration and head insertion, a contiguous mounted family DMC3-0.nbz through DMC3-N.nbz is traversed as N, N-1, ..., 0 before the earlier physical-root node. This precedence is mechanically derived from confirmed registration and traversal instructions, not from filename sorting.

locations.note: VA 0x140327430. Loads the global head at function entry, checks each node provider type, and advances with MOV RBX,[RBX+0x50].
Ascending registration order 0,1,2,... supplies the registration half of the effective reverse traversal proof.
Head insertion supplies the ordering half of the proof: each newly mounted higher index precedes all previously registered archives.
